impact:
Two bugs made every structured-data @id and url on the site unusable, defeating the SEO strategy that structured data exists to serve (rich snippets, Knowledge Graph, AI answer engines).

1. _url() in narrative/templatetags/seo_tags.py built "{scheme}://{request.get_host}{path}" — get_host without parentheses, so every @id read "https://<bound method HttpRequest.get_host of <WSGIRequest: GET '...'>>". 136 occurrences on a single series page. FIXED.

2. Narrative pages are served by custom views in narrative/urls.py rather than Wagtail page routing, so Page.url returns None for them; get_absolute_url() is the correct accessor. Roughly half the call sites already used get_absolute_url(); the rest passed .url and produced "https://hostNone". Fixed for character_jsonld (the character node and its affiliation Organization nodes) because the v2.6.0 affiliation work depends on it.

REMAINING: 20 call sites still pass .url — page.url in the series/season/episode/event tags, season.url, s.url, ancestor.url, p.character.url, page.episode.url, conn.from_event.url / conn.to_event.url, connection.from_event.url / connection.to_event.url. Each emits an @id ending in "None". They need the same .url -> get_absolute_url() treatment, plus a test asserting no @id contains "None" and every @id matches ^https?://[^/]+/. Worth auditing with Google's Rich Results Test afterwards, and re-checking Search Console once recrawled.
title: JSON-LD @ids are unresolvable sitewide: get_host not called, and .url is None for narrative pages
